944	### S9.3 Private store-instance lineage (successor; proposed, not accepted)
945	
946	A numeric store generation is not unique over time: `store-rollback` re-selects a
947	retained generation and `core-rollback` never raises the schema, so two physically
948	distinct stores can present the same `(storeGeneration, stateSchema)` pair. A
949	private **store instance identity** disambiguates them for local operational
950	records. It adds no member to `InstallationTransitionIntentV1`,
951	`InstallationTransitionJournalV1`, the namespace registry or any signed document,
952	introduces no envelope kind and no public major, and mints no D9 class, code or
953	exit; its refusals are the existing `TRANSITION.*` set and the existing
954	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` quarantine. It is never a wire field, an authority token or a
955	semantic input, and it never enters the pure evaluator or a Run hash.
956	
957	**Instance identity.** Each physical store instance carries one `storeInstanceId`:
958	32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from 128 bits of OS CSPRNG, allocated once
959	when that store is created, persisted in that store's own root before the store is
960	first published, and never rewritten. It has no ordering and no arithmetic, and
961	reading it grants nothing.
962	
963	**Lineage nodes, identified by the full triple.** A private append-only table
964	holds one node per admitted binding triple
965	`(storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema)`, carrying its predecessor triple
966	and the `intentDigest` of the transition that created it; both are `null` exactly
967	at a **lineage root**. Every lookup uses the whole triple, whose instance component
968	is read from the store-root **marker** of the store concerned: a numeric pair alone
969	never identifies a node, because a retained branch may lawfully present the same
970	pair as a fresh target. `intentDigest` is evidence validated *on* the selected node
971	and is never a search key, since it may lawfully repeat. This section asserts no
972	global uniqueness of a store generation beyond what the rules above already impose.
973	
974	**Marker observation is three-way and phase-bound.** Reading a store root yields
975	exactly one of: a **readable** identity; **absent**, meaning no store root is
976	present; or **unreadable**, meaning a root was observed but its marker is missing
977	or malformed. An unreadable marker is never treated as absence, and an absence must
978	be observed, never inferred from a missing observation. The store a transition
979	comes from always exists, so its marker is always required. The **selected**
980	store's marker is required only where the transition is settled as committed: at
981	`LEASED` and `PREPARING` a forward selection's target may not yet be materialised,
982	and after an abort an unpublished target may already have been reclaimed by the GC
983	census, so an absent target there is expected and must never be read as corruption.
984	
985	**One admission law.** A node is admitted only if its shape is admitted by the
986	private record's own closed schema, its predecessor and origin digest are null
987	together or present together, it does not name its own triple, its non-null
988	predecessor already exists as a node at that exact triple, no existing node shares
989	its primary key with disagreeing contents, and the chain from it is acyclic and
990	reaches exactly **one** lineage root. That root rule is scoped to the chain, not to
991	the whole table: an authorized restore or adoption starts its own lineage, so
992	several lineages may coexist. Publication and recovery apply this same law, and an
993	exact byte-identical match at the target key is idempotent but **not** a short
994	circuit — it is validated the same way and simply writes nothing. A refusal writes
995	nothing.
996	
997	**Selection case, derived from the admitted intent alone.** By the pair law in
998	S9.2 the case is decidable without reading any stored node: equal `to`/`from`
999	generation and schema is a **same-store** selection; an advanced schema is a
1000	**forward selection**; a retreated schema is an **ancestor re-selection**. Only a
1001	forward selection materialises a new store, allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`
1002	and writes one node, after the journal record is durably `COMMITTED` and never
1003	inside a level-4 grant-journal append lock. A same-store or ancestor re-selection
1004	writes no node: the store it selects already has one, created by an earlier act.
1005	
1006	**Recovery applies the same case, and only after the owner decides.**
1007	`recover_transition_journal` keeps every decision it already makes; this adds no
1008	state, code or recovery action, and in particular a core operation at `PREPARED`
1009	still aborts and a store operation still follows the S9 footprint. Where that
1010	function refuses, reports the project busy or quarantines, the companion makes **no
1011	decision at all**, inspects nothing and reads no marker. Where its action settles
1012	the transition as committed — `RESUME-COMMIT` or `RELEASE-ONLY` reaching `DONE` —
1013	then: a **forward selection** node must be present at its own full triple, or else
1014	reconstructed from the journal record's own from/to generation and schema members
1015	together with the predecessor and selected store-root markers, and admitted by the
1016	law above. A **same-store or ancestor** re-selection validates the retained node at
1017	its own full triple and **never rewrites its predecessor or origin digest**; an
1018	ancestor must additionally lie on the verified chain from the current node, so a
1019	store at a merely equal numeric pair off that chain never qualifies. That node was
1020	created by an earlier, unrelated act whose origin the current intent does not carry,
1021	so a missing one cannot be repaired from it and is `QUARANTINE` /
1022	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. No atomicity is claimed between the journal record and a node.
1023	
1024	**Before the owner settles a transition**, pre-existing ancestry is expected and
1025	untouched, including a retained branch at the same numeric generation, and an
1026	absent target is expected as above. Where a target *is* observable, what must not
1027	exist is a *new* node for that transition at **its own full triple**. For a forward
1028	selection, any node at that new target triple is premature. For a same-store or
1029	ancestor re-selection, the pre-existing node is expected; only a node claiming the
1030	current unrelated transition as its origin is contradictory. Each is a premature-node contradiction
1031	and quarantines; ordinary pre-existing lineage remains unchanged.
1032	
1033	**Lineage roots.** A root is created by an authorized local act that materialises a
1034	new physical store outside any transition: installation, or an authorized evidence
1035	restore or portable adoption. Such an act allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`,
1036	**replaces** any marker present in copied bytes before first publication so a
1037	restored store never impersonates its source, imports no node from the source, and
1038	imports no floor, grant or local commit authority. No transition is invented to
1039	give it an `intentDigest`.
1040	
1041	**Floors and authority are unchanged by this section.** An authorized transition
1042	keeps the S9 floor rules exactly: migration copies the floors forward into the new
1043	store, rollback inside the window sets them to the maximum of both stores, and a
1044	poisoned floor is lowered only by S4.5. An instance identity records which physical
1045	store is selected; it never lowers a floor and never confers local commit authority.

556 | F24 — Evidence ledger unreadable or wrong store selected | No reliable lookup conclusion | unknown-custody: Never interpret failed read, wrong generation or empty fallback DB as no commit. |

560 | F28 — Journal record pruned or unavailable after retained receipt | Historical record exists but required recovery custody cannot be reconstructed | unknown-custody: Never invent a journal proof or erase the historical receipt. Recovery metadata needs a retention root; lawful migrations preserve its verification lineage. |

561 | F29 — Reader observes transaction during publication | Committed snapshot excludes in-flight rows | unknown-attempt-open or committed-historically: Readers see old complete state or new complete state; no mixed receipt/association. A later valid PENDING journal append does not block confirmation of an earlier durable prefix. A snapshot missing an actively running requested attempt is not final absence. Apply the single-snapshot phase/outcome matrix; never infer terminal absence from an admitted attempt. The standing is selected from the one snapshot: admitted with neither row is unknown-attempt-open; a valid joined receipt is committed-historically (including pendingSettlement when admitted); a temporally skewed carrier capture that cannot reconcile within the bound is unavailable-busy. These are existing recovery standings, not a new snapshot-dependent public class. |

562 | F30 — Competing writer or EXCLUSIVE census while APPEND writer active | First admitted writer retains its guard | refused: Exercise actual process lock modes and S7 busy/retry behavior; no waiting/upgrades under the wrong lock. |

563 | F31 — Journal carrier cannot represent schema3 SEAL/current platform | Carrier incompatibility detected before commit work | refused: Explicit versioned migration required; never insert SEAL into the inherited SQL check set by disabling constraints. |

564 | F32 — Journal sequence reaches reserved terminal capacity | No ordinary SEAL in terminal slot | refused: Storage returns CarrierCapacityExhausted {grantGeneration, provenTailSeq} to host/finalization.rs. Host completes cleanup and releases the operation lease, then calls lifecycle under its fence to close/roll the generation. No storage-to-lifecycle reverse call, fence acquisition or rollover inside commit. |

577 | F45 — Prefix anchor with a PENDING witness at the tail carrying the tail body digest | The append became durable before the witness was advanced | committed-historically: The witness still names the durable tail, so it anchors it. Confirm for any requested sequence at or below the tail under anchor class witness-pending-at-tail, provided the witness bracket was byte-stable. Report witnessWouldAdvance as a diagnosis and perform no ADVANCE. The conclusion class is confirmed-under-retained-custody, never a cryptographic proof, and every confirming result carries the interior-bodies-not-authenticated diagnosis. |

578 | F46 — The generation holding the requested attempt is carrierFormat 1 or 2 | Historical generation in which no schema-3 SEAL row can exist | unknown-carrier-incompatible: Report carrier incompatibility, never not-committed and never uncommitted. Read historical bytes under recordSchema-1 semantics only; never relabel them as schema 3 and never present a historical platform alias as an S8 machine id. This is the read-side counterpart of F31. Note the measured scope: the inherited carrier refuses exactly the SEAL record type and the three alias-only machine platform ids, and admits the other eight schema-3 operational types. |

579 | F47 — Carrier-format migration from 1 or 2 to 3 | Inherited generation closed by TERMINAL; new carrierFormat 3 objects present | migrated: TERMINAL closes the inherited generation under the inherited constraints with no constraint or trigger disabled and no row rewritten. The TERMINAL row carries the migration operation own op- token, never a released analysis operation ref. Inherited rows and inherited schema objects stay byte-unchanged and legacy platform aliases are retained verbatim. A write to a generation below first_generation is refused. Run the whole transition under the install fence with non-blocking EXCLUSIVE on the affected project namespace. NO installation transition intent or journal is written: the closed 11-member intent and 20-member journal have no carrier field, reusing store-migrate is refused MIGRATE_REQUIRES_SCHEMA_ADVANCE and SCHEMA_CHANGE_SELECTS_NEW_STORE, and an invented carrier-migrate operation is refused by the closed operation enum. The footprint is self-describing from the three durable acts plus the operationRef already inside the frozen TERMINAL body. |

580 | F48 — Post-migration open and read dispatch, including a core that does not support carrierFormat 3 | carrierFormat 3 carrier present | refused: A carrierFormat-AWARE core that supports only formats 1 and 2 refuses a carrierFormat 3 carrier typed and keeps its prior generation until it expires, mirroring the S9 dual-reader staging. A FORMAT-UNAWARE core cannot be made to refuse at all, because it never looks for carrier_format; that limitation is selected and disclosed, detectable but not preventable, and its mitigation is the existing ordered-release discipline. A carrierFormat 1-2-3 core applies the selected dispatch in order: observe object NAMES only; refuse MIGRATION.CORRUPT on a partial name set; refuse MIGRATION.CORRUPT when all seven names are present but any definition is invalid; only then read the format row; then verify the frozen side-table SQL text, the carrier projectKeyDigest and the generation boundary; then read both historical and current generations without relabelling either. |

581 | F49 — Concurrency capture races during read-only recovery: a lawful concurrent APPEND-WRITE advances the witness, tail or floor between the reader's own observations, and a writer commits and exits after the reader's ledger snapshot | Carrier is entirely lawful; the reader's independently timed observations are mutually skewed, and its ledger snapshot may predate a commit that then completes | unavailable-busy: Two separate laws. First, an adverse witness or floor observation is a reportable owner quarantine condition only when both bracketing reads are byte-identical AND two journal snapshots agree on the tail sequence and tail digest; otherwise it is attributed to temporal skew and reported busy. A lawful later append must never produce a corruption diagnosis, and the reader must never invent one from independently timed observations. Second, terminality comes from the ledger-owned AttemptCustodyV1 phase read in the SAME snapshot as the receipt; no in-memory active set or separately timed liveness probe is consulted, so a stale snapshot plus later inactivity never yields a terminal not-committed conclusion. Bound the whole protocol to one ledger snapshot, at most two journal snapshots, at most four witness and four floor reads, no lock, no wait on the writer and no mutation. Exercise real concurrent processes, not only the model. |

582 | F50 — Carrier-format migration interrupted after any durable prefix of TERMINAL append, object creation and format-row publication | One-sided footprint: generation closed with no new objects; or objects present with no format row; or complete | resume-exact-prefix: Each of the three durable acts is atomic and the physical state is self-describing, so there is no torn state to repair. Act B is ONE explicit transaction on the same connection: BEGIN, every statement, COMMIT, ROLLBACK on failure. A bulk-script execution is NOT an acceptable act B, because it issues an implicit COMMIT and then runs statements one at a time, leaving earlier objects durable. Detection reads object NAMES first, refuses MIGRATION.CORRUPT on a partial set or on all-names-with-invalid-definitions, and reads the carrier_format ROW only after that, so objects without a published row still read as the inherited format. Prefix empty starts at A, or at B on a fresh install with no inherited table; prefix A resumes at B, recomputing the closed generation; prefix AB validates the existing definitions and resumes at C; prefix ABC is complete. first_generation is recomputed at C, never fixed earlier. COMMIT OR BARRIER UNCERTAINTY STOPS THE ATTEMPT: it performs cleanup only, releases EXCLUSIVE then the fence and writes nothing further; progress requires a separately admitted fresh maintenance attempt with its own migrationOpRef, re-acquiring fence and EXCLUSIVE, which resumes from the observed durable prefix. The same operation never retries an act or proceeds to the next. A TERMINAL naming a previous attempt operationRef is lawful history to resume past, never something to redo, and the inherited trigger independently refuses any append to a TERMINAL generation. Object existence is a resume signal, neve

583 | F51 — A format-unaware core opens or writes a migrated carrier | A generation at or above first_generation appears in the INHERITED table | split-brain-custody-condition: Prevention is impossible within the inherited format, which has no mechanism to refuse, and claiming otherwise would be an overclaim. Detection is exact: any generation at or above first_generation in the inherited table is a custody condition, never valid history, and is never merged into the current generation sequence. The mitigation is the existing ordered-release pattern, shipping the format-aware core first and enabling migration only once the selected core generation is at or above that release. For carrierFormat 1 the limit is wider because that format has no TERMINAL-closure trigger, so rows after the TERMINAL are also a custody condition. |

584 | F52 — Read-only recovery over every AttemptCustodyV1 phase and outcome against receipt and association presence | Any of the eleven settlement-matrix combinations, including a purged historical receipt | negative-only-from-settled-refused: terminal-not-committed requires ALL of: phase settled, settledOutcome exactly refused, and both the receipt and the association confirmed absent, in ONE coherent ledger snapshot. A settled-committed row with no receipt is a contradiction and unavailable history, never a negative. A receipt present while the attempt row is still admitted is the LAWFUL pre-settle interval, because the settle write is ordered after the receipt write: it answers committed-historically with pendingSettlement disclosed operationally, revives no authority, and no writer may reopen a stopped session merely to settle it. A present receipt with NO attempt-custody row and no legacy custody record answers committed-historically for commitment and custody-unknown-legacy for settlement, never a negative. Exactly one matrix cell yields the negative. A purged historical receipt never becomes never-committed: a logical retained tombstone or manifest that still names the Run is committed with degraded availability, which is a different observation from a raw both-absent snapshot, and no receipt is ever forged from a tombstone. There is no undetermined custody outcome: a durability-uncertain attempt stays admitted, and durability-undetermined is the D9 response to the caller. |

585 | F53 — The authorized settlement sweep over live, crashed, one-sided, inaccessible and already-settled attempts | Attempts left admitted by crashed, latching or durability-uncertain writers | settle-only-on-proof: The sweep runs as a per-namespace step of the existing store-gc operation under the install fence with non-blocking EXCLUSIVE, which is what proves no writer for the namespace is live. It reads ONE coherent ledger snapshot and writes only committed or refused, never undetermined, and at most one transition per attempt. It writes nothing when the lease is busy (skip and retain), when the ledger is unreadable, when the ledger is one-sided, or when the row is already settled. It reuses none of the dead attempt authority, obtains no new execution grant and never retries the commit. Permissible cleanup is the existing reachability GC of unreferenced orphan objects only; it may never synthesize a receipt or association, append a SEAL, raise the high-water, write or repair the witness, roll a grant generation or revive a grant. A failed, latching or durability-uncertain attempt must never open another write transaction with its stopped session; it releases and leaves the row admitted for the sweep. |

724	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,

727	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥
728	threshold + 1, namespaces present, no reuse of root keys) and up to 8 kernel
729	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
730	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
731	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
732	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
733	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
734	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.
735	
736	**Physical carrier bridge (carrierFormat).** The project grant-journal carrier has its
737	own format axis, and it is not the state schema. Detection on open is by schema
738	introspection only, because the oldest format carries no version row: object names
739	first, then refusal on a partial set, then definition validation, and the published
740	`carrier_format` row read **last**. Reader staging mirrors the root-reader and
741	state-decoder pattern, and its scope is stated precisely: a **carrierFormat-aware** core
742	that supports only {1, 2} refuses a carrierFormat 3 carrier **typed** and keeps its prior
743	generation until it expires; a carrierFormat {1, 2, 3} core reads both, under
744	recordSchema-1 semantics for historical generations and recordSchema-3 for current ones.
745	A **format-unaware** core cannot be made to refuse at all, because it never looks for

2	  grantGeneration INTEGER NOT NULL,
3	  seq          INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (seq >= 1 AND seq <= 9007199254740991),
4	  record_type  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (record_type IN
5	                 ('GRANT','NARROW','EXPIRY','RA','RCI','RCO','ICI','ICO','REV','CLN','AUD',
6	                  'CHECKPOINT','MIGRATION','TERMINAL')),
7	  operation_ref TEXT   NOT NULL CHECK (operation_ref GLOB 'op-[0-9a-f]*' AND length(operation_ref) = 35),
8	  request_ref  TEXT,
9	  token        TEXT,
10	  install_generation_id TEXT,
11	  manifest_digest TEXT CHECK (manifest_digest IS NULL OR length(manifest_digest) = 64),
12	  platform     TEXT CHECK (platform IS NULL OR platform IN ('macos-arm64','macos-x86_64','linux-x86_64','linux-arm64')),
13	  body         TEXT    NOT NULL,
14	  body_sha256  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(body_sha256) = 64),
15	  prev_sha256  TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(prev_sha256) = 64),
16	  CHECK (record_type <> 'GRANT' OR (install_generation_id IS NOT NULL AND manifest_digest IS NOT NULL AND platform IS NOT NULL AND token IS NOT NULL)),
17	  PRIMARY KEY (grantGeneration, seq)
18	) WITHOUT ROWID;
19	CREATE TRIGGER gj_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON grant_journal
20	  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal is append-only'); END;
21	CREATE TRIGGER gj_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON grant_journal
22	  BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal is append-only'); END;
23	CREATE TRIGGER gj_seq_contiguous BEFORE INSERT ON grant_journal
24	  BEGIN
25	    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.seq <> (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM grant_journal WHERE grantGeneration = NEW.grantGeneration)
26	      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal sequence must be tail+1') END;
27	    SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM grant_journal WHERE grantGeneration = NEW.grantGeneration AND record_type = 'TERMINAL')
28	      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal carrier is TERMINAL') END;
29	    SELECT CASE WHEN NEW.seq = 9007199254740991 AND NEW.record_type <> 'TERMINAL'
30	      THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'grant journal seq 9007199254740991 is the reserved terminal slot; roll the grant generation') END;
31	  END;

94	    files = {r["path"]: r for r in inventory["files"]}
95	    paths = set(files)

99	                       "workflowGoldens"}
100	    module_first = data["moduleFirstMilestone"]
101	    delivery_owners = {owner for group in delivery_groups for row in data["groups"][group]
102	                       for owner in row["owners"]}
103	    require(set(module_first) == delivery_owners
104	            and all(m in data["milestoneOrder"] for m in module_first.values()),
105	            "Missing/extra module milestone prerequisite")
106	    issues = {r["id"] for r in data["reviewIssues"]}
107	    for group, expected_rows in expected.items():
108	        rows = data["groups"][group]
109	        require(len(rows) == len({r["id"] for r in rows}), "Duplicate mapping: " + group)
110	        require({r["id"] for r in rows} == set(expected_rows),
111	                "Missing/extra source mapping: " + group)
112	        for row in rows:
113	            key, selector, value = expected_rows[row["id"]]
114	            require(row["source"] == {"key": key, "selector": selector,
115	                                      "valueSha256": digest(value)},
116	                    "Source selector/value drift: " + row["id"])
117	            require(row["milestone"] in {f"M{i}" for i in range(7)}, "Invalid milestone")
118	            require(row["owners"] and set(row["owners"]) <= paths,
119	                    "Missing inventory owner: " + row["id"])
120	            if group in {"commands", "queryOperations", "renderers"}:
121	                require(all(files[p]["role"] != "documentation" for p in row["owners"]),
122	                        "Runtime responsibility assigned to documentation: " + row["id"])
123	            if group in delivery_groups:
124	                require(all(row["milestone"] >= module_first[p] for p in row["owners"]),
125	                        "Delivery precedes module prerequisite: " + row["id"])
126	            verification = row["verification"]
127	            require(verification["owner"] in paths and verification["method"].strip(),
128	                    "Missing verification responsibility: " + row["id"])
129	            require(verification["standing"] == "not-executed",
130	                    "Planning cannot assert execution: " + row["id"])
131	            if verification["kind"] == "planned-behavioral-test":
132	                require(files[verification["owner"]]["role"] == "test",
133	                        "Behavioral verification requires a test owner: " + row["id"])
134	            elif files[verification["owner"]]["role"] == "documentation":
135	                require(verification["kind"] in {"qualification-harness-specification",
136	                        "section-owner-routing", "independent-review-scope"},
137	                        "Documentation is not an executable verification owner: " + row["id"])
138	            require(set(row["reviewIssues"]) <= issues, "Untracked review issue")
139	            if group == "capabilityCells":
140	                for field in ("state", "limitations", "deficiency", "corpusCases"):
141	                    require(row[field] == value[field], "Native matrix metadata drift")
142	                require(row["platformFamilies"] == sources["nativeMatrix"]["platformFamilies"],
143	                        "Missing platform population")
144	                require(row["qualificationMilestone"] == "M6", "Qualification milestone")
145	            if group == "commands":
146	                for field in ("requestClass", "authorizationClass", "formats", "parityFields"):
147	                    require(row[field] == value[field], "Command metadata drift")
148	            if group == "qualificationGates":
149	                for field in ("harness", "thresholdDisposition", "productExpansion"):
150	                    require(row[field] == value[field], "Gate metadata drift")
151	                require(row["qualificationMilestone"] == "M6", "Qualification milestone")
152	                require(row["inheritedAcceptance"] == value["acceptance"]
153	                        and row["gateOwner"] == value["owner"], "Gate standing/owner drift")
154	            if group == "workflowGoldens":
155	                require(row["command"] == value["command"]
156	                        and row["sourceClass"] == value["class"]
157	                        and row["sourceExitCode"] == value["exitCode"], "Golden source drift")
158	    renderer_milestones = {r["id"]: r["milestone"] for r in data["groups"]["renderers"]}
159	    command_milestones = {r["id"]: r["milestone"] for r in data["groups"]["commands"]}
160	    for row in data["groups"]["commands"]:
161	        require(all(row["milestone"] >= renderer_milestones[f] for f in row["formats"]),

163	    for row in data["groups"]["workflowGoldens"]:
164	        require(row["milestone"] >= command_milestones[row["command"]],

227	def render_recovery(data):
228	    lines = ["<!-- BEGIN GENERATED COMMIT RECOVERY -->", "",
229	             "| Private field | Representation | Exact binding |", "|---|---|---|"]
230	    for name, prop in data["recordSchema"]["properties"].items():
231	        lines.append(f"| `{name}` | `{data['fieldKinds'][name]}` | {cell(prop['description'])} |")
232	    lines += ["", "### Ordered failure matrix", "",
233	              "Conclusions below are internal scenario expectations, not new public D9",
234	              "codes. An unreadable or contradictory observation always prevents an",
235	              "uncommitted/committed conclusion. A missing receipt alone is not terminal",
236	              "absence: that requires settled+refused and both receipt and association",
237	              "absent in one coherent snapshot. No crash case has been executed.", "",
238	              "| Case / interruption | Possible stored state | Expected conclusion and action |",
239	              "|---|---|---|"]
240	    for c in data["cases"]:
241	        lines.append(f"| {c['id']} — {cell(c['checkpoint'])} | {cell(c['possibleStoredState'])} | "
242	                     f"{c['initialConclusion']}: {cell(c['expectedBehavior'])} |")
243	    lines += ["", "<!-- END GENERATED COMMIT RECOVERY -->"]
244	    return "\n".join(lines)

247	def replace_section(text, name, rendered):
248	    start, end = f"<!-- BEGIN GENERATED {name} -->", f"<!-- END GENERATED {name} -->"
249	    require(text.count(start) == text.count(end) == 1, "Missing/duplicate generated markers")
250	    a, b = text.index(start), text.index(end)
251	    require(a < b, "Reversed generated markers")
252	    return text[:a] + rendered + text[b + len(end):]

JSON edits are structural when the untouched file round-trips byte-exactly, otherwise exact text insertion,
and the result is re-parsed and compared with the intended structure. Refuses to run when a target already
differs from baseline. Emits proposed-edits.diff and before/after hashes.

    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


for rel in CHANGED:

    def hook(pairs):

343-
344-**Why a digest mismatch is not migration corruption.** A partial object set, an invalid definition, a
345-row before publication and a violated generation boundary are failures of the migration footprint
346-itself, so `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` names their remedy. A project digest mismatch leaves that footprint
347-intact: the carrier at this namespace carries another project's binding. The frozen v8 witness law
348-already treats the same fact as a carrier quarantine, and S12 keeps journal-carrier quarantine free of
349-`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` so that one code never carries two remedies. On read-only recovery the
350-association's own carrier naming decides first: an association that names another carrier is the
351-existing `binding-unusable` refusal of the recovery request.
352-
353-**Why F46 is `HOST.IO_FAILURE`.** An association is written only with a committed carrierFormat 3
354-`SEAL`, so one naming a historical generation contradicts two retained owners. That is the
355-`unknown-custody` family (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`, `host-io`): not a caller defect (request-rejected), not a
356-stably observed quarantine (`LEDGER.CORRUPT`) and not contention. It never becomes not-committed or a
357-confirmation.
358-
359-**Interrupted state and stale custody.** Each phase re-evaluates every predicate from the bytes it
360-reads at that open or in that journal snapshot: a cached verdict, `first_generation`,
361-`projectKeyDigest` or earlier successful open is never reused. A writer or maintenance refusal appends
362-nothing, publishes nothing and writes no marker, because `carrier_quarantine.reason` keeps its inherited
363-enum; the next open detects the same condition again. Read-only recovery writes nothing, uses
364-`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` on no path, and reports the quarantine-condition row only with its Step 4 stable
365-observations, otherwise `unavailable-busy`. A lawful `{A}` or `{A, B}` prefix stays a resumable
366-interrupted migration, never a corruption diagnosis. No route confirms, negates or settles an attempt,
367-merges split-brain rows, rewrites the immutable format row or grants authority.
368-

371-Every generation lives entirely in exactly one table, and generations are totally ordered per
372-project, so the union is unambiguous.

"""Show the new source37 controls discriminate: run the EDITED validator over two hybrid trees that restore baseline
bytes for exactly one remedy area each, and record which checks fail.

  hybrid-ddl     edited tree, but baseline grant-journal.carrier.v3.sql and attempt-custody.schema.v1.json
                 (expect source37 grammar / publication / scenario failures; route rows still agree)
  hybrid-routes  edited tree, but baseline security-and-lifecycle.md and commit-recovery-readonly.v3.md
                 (expect source37 S12 / read-only row failures; DDL controls still pass)

Hybrids are new disposable directories; baseline and edited copies are only read.
"""
import hashlib, json, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path('/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/claude-source37-carrier-owner-author.v1')
BL, ED = BASE / 'work/baseline', BASE / 'work/edited'
HYBRIDS = {
    'hybrid-ddl': ['docs/coop/design-corrections/security/grant-journal.carrier.v3.sql',
                   'docs/v2/architecture/attempt-custody.schema.v1.json'],
    'hybrid-routes': ['docs/v2/contracts/product-v1/security-and-lifecycle.md',
                      'docs/v2/architecture/commit-recovery-readonly.v3.md'],
}
result = {}
for name, restore in HYBRIDS.items():
    root = BASE / 'work' / name
    shutil.copytree(ED, root, symlinks=True, dirs_exist_ok=False)
    for rel in restore:
        shutil.copyfile(BL / rel, root / rel)
    report = BASE / 'receipts' / ('p06-integrated-carrier.' + name + '.json')
    if report.exists():
        raise SystemExit('preserve earlier report: ' + str(report))
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', str(root / 'docs/coop/design-corrections/security/check-integrated-carrier.v1.py'),
                        '--source', str(root), '--report', str(report)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
    rep = json.loads(report.read_text()) if report.exists() else {'error': r.stderr[-2000:]}
    failures = [c['check'] for c in rep.get('checks', []) if not c['pass']]
    result[name] = {
        'restoredBaselineFiles': {rel: hashlib.sha256((root / rel).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for rel in restore},
        'childExit': r.returncode, 'passed': rep.get('passed'), 'failed': rep.get('failed'),
        'failures': failures, 'allFailuresAreSource37Controls': bool(failures) and all(f.startswith('source37') for f in failures),
        'error': rep.get('error'),
    }
ddl_fail = result['hybrid-ddl']['failures']
route_fail = result['hybrid-routes']['failures']
result['expectations'] = {
    'hybrid-ddl fails grammar controls': any('refuses an uppercase or non-hex' in f for f in ddl_fail),
    'hybrid-ddl fails publication controls': any('refuses every grant_journal_v3 append' in f for f in ddl_fail),
    'hybrid-ddl fails first_generation coupling': any('first_generation is exactly 1' in f for f in ddl_fail),
    'hybrid-ddl fails interrupted-state scenarios': any(f.startswith('source37 scenario') for f in ddl_fail),
    'hybrid-ddl keeps route rows agreeing': not any('S12 row' in f or 'section 1 row' in f for f in ddl_fail),
    'hybrid-routes fails S12 row controls': any('S12 row' in f for f in route_fail),
    'hybrid-routes fails read-only table controls': any('section 1 row' in f for f in route_fail),
    'hybrid-routes keeps DDL controls passing': not any('grant_journal_v3.' in f or 'attempt_custody' in f for f in route_fail),
    'only source37 controls fail': result['hybrid-ddl']['allFailuresAreSource37Controls'] and result['hybrid-routes']['allFailuresAreSource37Controls'],
}
(BASE / 'receipts' / 'p06-control-discrimination.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
if not all(result['expectations'].values()):
    raise SystemExit(1)

# Source37 carrier owner correction: A37-01 to A37-04

**Standing.** This is a bounded coauthor owner correction by an actual Claude session. It is not acceptance, not independent review, and not implementation or durability qualification.

- **Scope of writes.** Everything lives in this new runtime. Frozen and live historical bytes were only read.
- **Not done:** edits to source-pins ledgers or generated planning outputs; freeze, activation, commit or push; product code.
- **Recovery cases.** All 54 product recovery cases (F00–F53) remain **not-executed**.

**Source.** `candidate-subject.v37`, manifest SHA-256 `245ef613…91676680`.
- Verified in p00: 29 read, edited or run files agree with their exact manifest pins.
- p04 re-verified frozen and baseline bytes after all work.

## Owner law checked before any route was chosen

- **S12 rows (security-and-lifecycle.md:1300–1308):**
  - `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` → operational-failed/4/`LEDGER.CORRUPT`.
  - Read-only stable quarantine → `LEDGER.CORRUPT`/`ledger-corrupt` with `domainDetail` omitted.
  - Read-only unreadable, unobserved or unreachable anchor → `HOST.IO_FAILURE`/`host-io`.
  - Read-only foreign carrier or swapped store/namespace → request-rejected/2/`EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED` (`RECOVERY.REFUSED`).
  - `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` is not reused for ordinary journal corruption.
- **Security model D9 map:** `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` and `RECOVERY.REFUSED` carry exactly those triples.
- **Frozen v8 `reconcile_witness`:** a witness naming another project key returns QUARANTINE, *witness names another carrier*.
- **Read-only v3:** §1 standings; §3 routes a foreign witness to `unknown-quarantine-condition`; Step 4 requires stable observations before any quarantine report.
- **D9 v1.14:** codeMaps `ledger-corrupt↔LEDGER.CORRUPT`, `host-io↔HOST.IO_FAILURE`, `ledger-busy↔LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT`, and `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED` is a rejection code. nonAnalysisDerivation rule 5 makes datastore failures operational-failed.
- **carrier-migration §4:** a lawful `{A}` or `{A, B}` prefix is busy/unavailable on read-only, never corruption.

## Dispositions

### A37-01: CORRECTED in the owner DDL
- **Change.** Every hex-bearing carrierFormat 3 column now checks lowercase hex over its whole hex part: prefix `GLOB`, exact length, then `substr(col, prefix+1) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'`.
  - `carrier_format.project_key_digest`, `migration_op_ref`;
  - `grant_journal_v3.operation_ref`, `run_id`, `manifest_digest`, `body_sha256`, `prev_sha256`.
  - The planned private `attempt_custody` DDL applies the same law to `store_generation_digest`, `execution_id` and `operation_ref`.
- **Authority.** Host record admission still owns the record bodies; the DDL is defence in depth.
- **Historical scope.** carrierFormat 1 and 2 bytes stay frozen and still check only the first character, which p01b records.
  - This is disclosed, not repaired: historical rows are read only as history, never pass the schema-3 gate, and can never satisfy a schema-3 SEAL join (F46).
  - The earlier proposed v3 and attempt-custody bytes were never instantiated and are superseded in place.

### A37-02: CORRECTED in the DDL and the protocol
- **DDL.**
  - `gj3_append_laws` refuses every append while no `carrier_format` row exists.
  - A CHECK couples `first_generation` to `migrated_from`: exactly 1 on the fresh path, at least 2 when migrated.
- **Act C (fresh, or resuming `{A, B}`).** It verifies three things in the publishing transaction and publishes nothing if any fails:
  - the seven definitions;
  - an empty `grant_journal_v3`;
  - a surviving witness that names the admitted project digest.
- **Published carriers.** A new row-level check (3a) refuses any `grant_journal_v3` row below `first_generation`.
- The seven object names are unchanged.
- **Why both of the review's options.** The DDL prevents the append on a lawful footprint; the publication and row checks verify rows that did not come through that law.

### A37-03: CORRECTED with phase-specific routes
A published `project_key_digest`, or a witness, that names another project is a **carrier project binding mismatch**, not migration corruption. The migration footprint itself is intact, the frozen v8 law already calls this a carrier quarantine, and S12 keeps one remedy per code.

| Phase | Observation | Route |
|---|---|---|
| writer or maintenance open; act C publication | carrier's own binding names another project | operational-failed / 4 / `LEDGER.CORRUPT` / `ledger-corrupt`, `domainDetail` omitted; nothing appended or published |
| writer or maintenance open; act C publication | partial objects, invalid definitions, v3 rows before publication, violated published boundary (incl. F51) | operational-failed / 4 / `LEDGER.CORRUPT` / `ledger-corrupt`, detail `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` |
| read-only recovery | association's `journalCarrierDigest`, `storeGenerationDigest` or `namespaceId` differs from the admitted binding | `binding-unusable`: request-rejected / 2 / `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`, `RECOVERY.REFUSED` (existing S12 row) |
| read-only recovery | association names the admitted carrier, but the carrier's own binding names another project, or the footprint is unlawful, or F51 | `unknown-quarantine-condition`: `LEDGER.CORRUPT` / `ledger-corrupt`, omitted; requires Step 4, otherwise `unavailable-busy` |

`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` is used on **no** read-only path.

### A37-04: CORRECTED, routes assigned
- **F46 `unknown-carrier-incompatible`:** operational-failed / 4 / `HOST.IO_FAILURE` / `host-io`, `domainDetail` omitted. It is never not-committed and never a confirmation.
  - An association is written only with a committed carrierFormat 3 SEAL, so one naming a historical generation contradicts two retained owners. That places it in the `unknown-custody` family.
  - It is not a caller defect and not a stable quarantine.
  - The comparison uses `first_generation` read in the same journal snapshot.
- **F51 `split-brain-custody-condition`:**
  - At a writer or maintenance open, `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` (the existing post-detection boundary check).
  - On read-only recovery, the quarantine-condition row under Step 4, otherwise `unavailable-busy`.
  - It is re-detected at every open, writes nothing, and never merges rows.
- **Where recorded:** new S12 rows, the read-only §1 row and paragraph, carrier-format §8.1, and dispatch `publicProjectionByPhase`.
- **Unchanged:** the plan case records in `commit-recovery-plan.v1.json` and `carrier-fault-cases.v1.json` keep their standings, so the generated failure matrix does not change.

### Other advisories
- **A37-05 and A37-06:** not owned (root, query). No edit.
- **A37-07:** owned wording corrected; build-plan lines routed to root.
  - Current-standing notes were added to carrier-format.v3.md, commit-recovery-readonly.v3.md and carrier-migration.v1.md; the Source25 baseline is not relabelled.
  - store-instance-lineage.v1.json gained a note that the current plan holds F00–F53.
  - The build-plan lines 10, 19, 1041, 1045 and 1085 are root's.
- **A37-08:** not owned (native registered-schema successor). No edit.
- **S37-01/02/03:** not owned. No edit.
- **Termination R1/R2:** not extended.
  - Every carrier route validates under both the current and the R1/R2 StepTermination (p05).
  - The new request-rejected code check covers only the carrier `binding-unusable` route and asserts no global rejection-code partition. The `finding.show` HOST.IO_FAILURE exit-2 route is untouched.

## Interrupted migration, recovery and authority
- **No cached state.** Every predicate is re-read from the bytes of that open or that journal snapshot. No cached verdict, `first_generation`, `projectKeyDigest` or earlier successful open is ever reused.
- **Refusals write nothing.** Writer and maintenance refusals append, publish and mark nothing; `carrier_quarantine.reason` keeps its inherited enum.
- **Interrupted prefixes stay resumable.** A lawful `{A}` or `{A, B}` prefix remains a resumable migration: the reader reports busy, and a fresh admitted attempt resumes at C under its own lease.
- **No authority granted.** No route confirms, negates or settles an attempt, merges split-brain rows, rewrites the immutable format row, or grants authority.

## Exact edits
`proposed-edits.diff` (SHA-256 `806c785e04c61fa2fcc8b47939319d25109d9e648f25ce65a176d67090af6758`, 1097 lines) covers 9 files.

| File | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| security/grant-journal.carrier.v3.sql | `23902324…` | `f0a22382…` |
| security/carrier-format.v3.md | `04e6271d…` | `0095e61a…` |
| security/carrier-migration.v1.md | `0295d5e0…` | `446c73dc…` |
| security/carrier-dispatch.v3.json | `0603be7f…` | `55d5597d…` |
| security/check-carrier-v3.py | `137f5cb7…` | `37f370b0…` |
| architecture/attempt-custody.schema.v1.json | `37f1445c…` | `eb1e8755…` |
| architecture/commit-recovery-readonly.v3.md | `a60b048c…` | `3b32d24a…` |
| architecture/store-instance-lineage.v1.json | `2ff48b40…` | `919d1717…` |
| contracts/product-v1/security-and-lifecycle.md | `42bafae6…` | `9ca85de1…` |

Full hashes are in `review.json` and `receipts/p02-apply-edits.json`.

## Controls and receipts
- **p01 / p01b, the review's carrier probe replayed.**
  - Baseline reproduces the review exactly: every non-hex tail ADMITs, and a generation-1 append before publication is published below `first_generation`.
  - Edited: every grammar violation and every pre-publication append refuses. The review's exact format row (first_generation 5 with no migration fields) is itself refused, by design.
  - p01's crash on the edited copy (it did not catch a refused format row) is **preserved**; p01b replaces it.
- **p03, owner validator `check-integrated-carrier.v1.py`.** Baseline 87/0; edited **201/0**, with 114 new source37 controls:
  - SQLite admission for every hex column;
  - the publication and `first_generation` law;
  - an executable open dispatch over real carrier states: interrupted fresh `{B}` and migrated `{A, B}`, act C resume, foreign witness, foreign published digest, association mismatch, F46, F51 re-detected after a clean open, partial or invalid definitions, and rows below first;
  - every projection checked against the selected StepTermination schema, D9 codeMaps, the security model map, S12 rows and the read-only §1 table.
- **p05.** All nine routes are admitted by both the current and the R1/R2 StepTermination schemas and are D9-legal.
- **p06, discrimination.** The edited validator was run over hybrid trees:
  - with the baseline DDL restored, **25** source37 failures;
  - with the baseline S12 and read-only table restored, **5** route-row failures;
  - no pre-existing check failed in either.
- **p04, drift for root.** Frozen and baseline bytes are unchanged, and no other file in the edited tree differs.

## Report to root: bindings that drift until rebind
Computed by p04, not executed:
- **Candidate37 manifest pins:** all 9 files.
- **implementation-normative-inputs.v5:** 8 files (all but check-carrier-v3.py).
- **implementation-coverage sources:** 8.
- **Planning contractSections:** `security-and-lifecycle:12` value and selector drift; `:13`–`:16` selector drift only (line shift).
- **Source-pins ledgers:** foundation evaluator3/foundation/native/security/workflows, all 9 files in each.
- **Expected checker failures until rebind:** reference-group pin checks, the planning checker and package verification.
- **Unchanged:** the generated commit-recovery section and its inputs.

## Limits
- **Reference only.** In-memory SQLite plus a reference dispatch; no OS durability, crash, lock, process or on-disk behaviour. F00–F53 remain not-executed.
- **Witness and stability not simulated.** Witness digests are supplied as parameters, and the Step 4 stability rule is asserted as data law without simulating bracket timing.
- **Act B atomicity not re-exercised.** Rows before publication or below first were injected by lifting and reinstalling the append trigger with byte-identical text (disclosed harness).
- **Historical measurements.** C1–C18 were not rerun, and their evidence is not in the repository.
- **Suites not run.** Reference groups, pin verification, the planning checker and package verification were not run.
- **Discrimination gaps.**
  - p06 does not test the widened wording inside the two existing S12 rows; their class, exit and code are unchanged.
  - Some hybrid-ddl scenario failures cascade from the admitted append.
- **Whole-carrier swap.** A swap that carries a consistent foreign witness and floor stays in the already-disclosed undetected whole-root substitution class.
- **No new marker.** No durable quarantine marker was added, so refusals are re-detected at each open.
- **identity-and-evidence.md** was not edited; it has no route rows and does not contradict these routes.
- **F46 → HOST.IO_FAILURE** is a reasoned selection among existing rows; root owns whether to adopt it.
- **Not acceptance.** An independent review of the corrected bytes is still required.

All subprocesses ran in the foreground and have completed; no background process was started.

I've written owner corrections for A37-01 through A37-04 in a disposable copy only. The owner's carrier validator passes 201/0 on the corrected copy, up from 87/0 on baseline, with 114 new checks. This is not acceptance: all 54 product recovery cases (F00–F53) are still not executed, and the new checks are in-memory SQLite reference controls, not durability testing.

**A37-01, lowercase-hex grammar.**
- **Change:** every hex column in the v3 journal DDL and the private attempt-custody DDL now checks the whole hex part, not just the first character.
- **Evidence:** replaying the review's probe, every non-hex or uppercase value that baseline admitted is now refused.
- **Historical scope:** the frozen v1/v2 carrier bytes are unchanged and keep the weak check. That limit is disclosed, not repaired: historical rows are read only as history and can never satisfy a schema-3 SEAL join. The earlier v3 bytes were never instantiated, so they are corrected in place.

**A37-02, first_generation at publication and {A,B} resume.**
- **DDL:** the append trigger refuses any row while no `carrier_format` row exists. A new CHECK makes `first_generation` exactly 1 on a fresh install and at least 2 after migration.
- **Act C (fresh or resuming {A,B}):** in the publishing transaction it verifies the seven definitions, an empty `grant_journal_v3`, and that any surviving witness names the admitted project. If any check fails, nothing is published.
- **Published carriers:** a new row-level check refuses any v3 row below `first_generation`.
- No new objects; the seven object names are unchanged.

**A37-03, project binding mismatch vs migration corruption.** I kept each route consistent with existing S12, the frozen v8 witness law ("witness names another carrier") and the D9 code maps.

| Phase | Observation | Route |
|---|---|---|
| Writer/maintenance open or act C | Carrier's own digest or witness names another project | operational-failed / 4 / `LEDGER.CORRUPT` / `ledger-corrupt`, no detail, nothing written |
| Writer/maintenance open or act C | Partial objects, invalid definitions, rows before publication, broken generation boundary | same class and code, detail `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` |
| Read-only recovery | The association names another carrier | existing `binding-unusable`: request-rejected / 2 / `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`, `RECOVERY.REFUSED` |
| Read-only recovery | Association matches, but the carrier's binding or footprint is wrong | quarantine row (`LEDGER.CORRUPT`, no detail), only with stable observations, otherwise busy |

`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` is never used on a read-only path.

**A37-04, F46 and F51.**
- **F46 (`unknown-carrier-incompatible`):** operational-failed / 4 / `HOST.IO_FAILURE` / `host-io`, no detail. Associations are only written with a committed v3 SEAL, so one naming an older generation is a contradiction between two records. That puts it with the existing unknown-custody row; it never becomes "not committed" or a confirmation. This is my selection among existing rows, and root decides whether to keep it.
- **F51 (split-brain):** `MIGRATION.CORRUPT` at a writer or maintenance open (the existing generation-boundary check). On read-only recovery it is the quarantine row, otherwise busy. It is re-detected at every open and never merged.
- **Where recorded:** rows added to S12, the read-only §1 table, carrier-format §8.1 and the dispatch JSON. The recovery-plan case records are unchanged, so the generated build-plan failure table doesn't move.

Interrupted migration is preserved: every check re-reads the current bytes (no cached verdict), refusals write nothing, a lawful {A}/{A,B} prefix stays resumable, and no route grants authority.

**How the controls were proven:**
- **Discrimination:** running the new validator with the old DDL restored produces 25 failures; restoring the old S12 and read-only table produces 5. Only the new checks fail in either case.
- **R1/R2 compatibility:** all nine routes are valid under both the current StepTermination schema and the R1/R2-tightened one. I did not extend R1/R2. The new request-rejected code check covers only the carrier route and asserts no global partition, so `finding.show`'s exit-2 route is untouched.
- **Kept failure:** the first probe replay crashed on the corrected copy because the review's exact format row is now refused and the probe didn't catch that. The corrected replay (p01b) records it instead.

**Other advisories:**
- **A37-07:** current-standing notes added to carrier-format, the read-only doc, carrier-migration and store-instance-lineage (current plan is F00–F53), without relabelling the Source25 history. The build-plan lines are yours.
- **Not touched:** A37-05, A37-06, A37-08 and S37-01..03 are not mine.

**Report of changed files for root (drift computed, checkers not run):**
- **Changed:** 9 files: the v3 SQL, carrier-format, carrier-migration, carrier-dispatch, check-carrier-v3, attempt-custody schema, commit-recovery-readonly, store-instance-lineage, security-and-lifecycle.
- **Bindings that drift until rebind:**
  - the candidate37 manifest pins all 9 files;
  - normative-inputs v5 binds 8 (all but the checker);
  - 8 planning coverage sources;
  - planning section S12 changes value, and S13–S16 shift line numbers only;
  - 5 source-pins ledgers each list all 9.
- **Unchanged:** generated planning inputs, all pin ledgers, and the frozen source.
- **Consequence:** pin checks, the planning checker and package verification will report drift until rebind.

**Limits not covered above:**
- **Not simulated:** witness and floor timing, act B atomicity (rows were injected with a disclosed trigger-lift harness), and the historical C1–C18 measurements.
- **Wording not discriminated:** the widened text inside the two existing S12 rows isn't tested; their class, exit and code are unchanged.
- **Whole-carrier swap:** a swap with a consistent foreign witness stays in the already-disclosed undetectable class.

All subprocesses ran in the foreground and have finished.

Files are in `/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/claude-source37-carrier-owner-author.v1/` (probes and receipts are in the same folder):
- `review.md` (`ad694331…`)
- `review.json` (`e83f6a77…`)
- `proposed-edits.diff` (`806c785e…`, 1097 lines; before/after hashes in `review.json`)
